principles: User task clarity is more important than visual novelty.
Product components consume semantic tokens instead of raw palette values.
Shared component APIs express intent rather than low-level styling.
One section should normally contain no more than one dominant primary action.
Responsive behavior must be defined by component and layout contracts.
Loading, empty, warning, error, unavailable, and permission states are first-class interface requirements.
Technical backend identifiers must not appear directly in ordinary user-facing content.
Accessibility behavior belongs in shared components whenever possible.

mono.value: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, monospace
mono.description: Monospaced font for technical identifiers when approved.

sm.description: Default label and compact body text.

3xl.description: Large page title when explicitly approved.
restrictions: Do not use for dense operational pages without design-direction approval.

usage: Only for expressive or explicitly approved hero moments.
Important inline or compact data text.
Field labels and compact control labels.
Subordinate timestamps, IDs, and descriptive metadata.
Approved technical identifiers and code-like values.

spacingRelations.notes: Gap between elements that explain one another.

rules: Declare key lines for page content, section content, repeated rows, and action groups.
Do not align visual groups by eye when grid, flex, or layout primitives can express the relationship.
One dominant focal point per state and viewport unless an approved exception exists.
Color cannot be the only signal of hierarchy.
WCAG contrast is the minimum legibility gate, not proof of hierarchy.
Primary, supporting, contextual, and audit information must remain distinguishable without relying only on color.
Do not scale font size directly with viewport width.
Responsive changes preserve reading order, action priority, and content priority.

primary.intent: Dominant action that advances the primary task.
prohibitedUse: Several competing actions in one section.

allowedUse: Alternative action near the primary action.
Export or utility action when prominence is justified.

prohibitedUse: Primary submission when a primary action exists.
Only visible call to action in an empty state.

sm.intent: Compact toolbar and dense table action.

slots.name: leadingIcon
slots.description: Optional decorative or semantic icon before the label.

slots.name: label
slots.description: Visible action label unless the icon-only size is used.

slots.name: trailingIcon
slots.description: Optional directional or disclosure icon after the label.

props.name: loading
props.description: Displays pending feedback and prevents duplicate activation.

useWhen: The user must invoke an action.
The action has a clear semantic priority.
doNotUseWhen: Navigation should be represented by a standard link.
compositionRules: A section normally contains no more than one primary button.
Destructive buttons must not use the primary variant.
Icon-only buttons require an accessible name.

contentRules.wrapping: Button labels should remain short. Allow wrapping only when the approved layout requires it.
contentRules.truncation: Do not truncate critical action labels.
contentRules.localization: Allow reasonable text expansion without fixed-width assumptions.
contentRules.emptyContent: A button must not render without an accessible label.

accessibility.semanticElement: button unless the control is genuine navigation
keyboard: Do not activate while disabled or loading.
accessibility.accessibleName: Visible label or explicit aria-label for icon-only usage.
aria: Use aria-disabled only when native disabled is unsuitable.
Use aria-busy when loading behavior requires announcement.
announcements: Pending state should be perceivable when action duration is meaningful.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Danger and warning meaning must also be communicated by text, icon, or context.

responsive.strategy: Preserve semantic priority while allowing actions to wrap or move into overflow.
responsive.narrowBehavior: Primary action may become full width in forms and onboarding. Secondary utilities may move to overflow.
responsive.wideBehavior: Actions remain content-width and align according to the owning layout.
responsive.overflow: Button labels must not create page-level overflow.

allowedUse: Search fields when composed with SearchInput.
prohibitedUse: Selection from a constrained option list.

useWhen: The user must enter one line of textual or numeric content.
doNotUseWhen: A constrained option selector is more appropriate.
compositionRules: Compose with the canonical FormField for label, help, and error behavior.
Placeholder text must not replace a visible label.

contentRules.maximum: Length must follow the feature schema.
contentRules.localization: Labels and help text must support expansion.
contentRules.emptyContent: Empty value must remain distinguishable from unavailable data.

aria: Use aria-describedby for help and error text.
announcements: Validation messages must be programmatically associated.
accessibility.colorIndependence: Invalid state must include text, not only color.

responsive.strategy: Width is owned by the form layout rather than the primitive.
responsive.narrowBehavior: May become full width within the form group.
responsive.wideBehavior: Width should reflect expected content when the form recipe supports columns.
responsive.overflow: Must not exceed the parent container.

layoutRecipes.description: Evidence-based human review and approval workspace.

rules: Product screens consume semantic colors.
Status meaning must use the matching semantic status role.
The primary brand color is reserved for primary actions, focus, and approved emphasis.
prohibited: Raw hex colors inside product components.
Tailwind palette colors directly inside route-level JSX.
Danger colors used decoratively.
Color as the only status indicator.
exceptions: Brand assets may preserve approved embedded colors.
Third-party visualizations may use a documented chart palette.

rules: Use the approved spacing scale.
The parent layout owns spacing between sibling elements.
Use gap-based composition for repeated layouts.
prohibited: Arbitrary spacing without documented reason.
Simultaneous parent gap and child margins for the same relationship.
Large empty regions without structural purpose.

rules: Use semantic text styles.
Use restrained headings in operational screens.
Use tabular numerals where numeric comparison benefits.
prohibited: Page-specific heading scales.
Excessively light weights for important information.
Uppercase labels used indiscriminately.

rules: Search the catalog before creating a component.
Extend canonical components through approved variants.
Register stable shared components with a contract, stories, and tests.
Use semantic props rather than low-level style props.
prohibited: Components named NewButton, BetterCard, ModernInput, or ComponentV2.
Duplicated canonical primitives.
Page-local reimplementations of registered shared components.
Shared components containing feature-specific API requests.

rules: Responsive transformation is defined in the component or layout contract.
Validate rendered behavior at approved viewports.
Use internal scrolling only where the pattern explicitly permits it.
prohibited: Page-level horizontal overflow.
Fixed-width assumptions that break localization.
Claiming responsiveness based only on Tailwind class presence.

rules: Use native semantics before ARIA.
Every interactive control has an accessible name.
Focus-visible state is mandatory.
Validation errors are programmatically associated.
prohibited: Important actions available only on hover.
Placeholder-only labels.
Color-only state communication.
Interactive div elements without valid semantics.

rules: Use real or domain-plausible content.
Test long labels, long values, empty values, and unavailable values.
Translate backend identifiers through a presentation layer.
prohibited: Lorem ipsum in product screens.
Raw snake_case or camelCase values in ordinary user interfaces.
Raw ISO timestamps displayed directly.
Critical content truncated without access to the full value.

rules: Motion communicates state, continuity, or progress.
Respect reduced-motion preferences.
Use approved duration and easing tokens.
prohibited: Decorative animation that delays interaction.
Unapproved custom durations.
Continuous motion without operational value.

rules: Use the approved icon library.
Icon-only controls require an accessible name.
Decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology.
prohibited: Mixing icon libraries without approval.
Information icons beside every label.
Unlabeled icon-only actions.

rules: Form fields use canonical label, help, error, disabled, and read-only patterns.
Field widths reflect content expectations and the approved form recipe.
Primary submission and destructive actions remain semantically distinct.
prohibited: Placeholder text replacing labels.
Every field stretched to maximum page width.
Validation communicated only through border color.

rules: Metric groups distinguish critical, financial, operational, and informational data.
Tables define column priority and responsive behavior.
Numerical alignment supports comparison.
prohibited: Large grids of equally prominent metrics.
Table actions visually dominating the data.
Cards used as the default container for every value.

checks.description: The machine-readable design system must validate against its JSON schema.
checks.remediation: Correct invalid fields or update the schema through an approved design-system change.

checks.description: Product components must not contain unapproved literal colors.
checks.remediation: Replace the literal value with an approved semantic token.

checks.description: Arbitrary Tailwind spacing, radius, typography, and z-index values require documented approval.
checks.remediation: Use an approved token or document the integration-specific exception.

checks.description: Canonical primitives must not be duplicated.
checks.remediation: Use or extend the registered canonical component.

checks.description: Interactive controls must have accessible names and visible focus behavior.
checks.remediation: Correct component semantics, labels, and focus-visible styles.

checks.description: Rendered screens must not introduce unexpected page-level horizontal overflow.
checks.remediation: Correct the owning layout or component responsive contract.

checks.description: Stable shared components should have approved component contracts and Storybook coverage.
checks.remediation: Create the missing contract and meaningful component stories.

checks.description: Destructive actions must use approved destructive semantics.
checks.remediation: Use the danger variant, confirmation pattern, and approved content.

checks.description: Backend identifiers and raw technical errors must not be exposed to ordinary users.
checks.remediation: Map the value through the approved terminology, formatter, or error layer.
